hints: Focus on what actually happens to the double bond when ethene joins together to make poly(ethene).
Ethene has $sp^2$ carbons with $120^\circ$ angles and a $C=C$ double bond, while poly(ethene) has $sp^3$ carbons with about $109^\circ$ angles and only $C-C$ single bonds.
Remember that every covalent bond has one sigma component, so ask yourself which type of bond must survive polymerisation.
walkthrough:
**Recall the bonding in ethene**

Think of ethene as flat with a double bond. Each carbon is $sp^2$ with bond angles of about $120^\circ$.

Chemical structure:
$$\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2$$

**Recall the bonding in poly(ethene)**

During addition polymerisation the $\pi$ part of the $C=C$ breaks to form new $C-C$ links. The chain is saturated, so each carbon is $sp^3$ with angles of about $109^\circ$.

Polymer repeat:
$$- [\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2]_n -$$

**Find what is common to both**

Both molecules contain $C-H$ bonds and $C-C$ bonds. Every single bond is a $\sigma$ bond, and every double bond is one $\sigma$ plus one $\pi$.

Rule to remember:
$$\text{single bond = 1 } \sigma, \quad \text{double bond = 1 } \sigma + 1 \pi$$

**Make the deduction**

$\pi$ bonds, $120^\circ$ angles and $sp^2$ are lost on polymerisation. $109^\circ$ angles and $sp^3$ are only gained in the polymer. The $\sigma$ framework is present in both, so that is the shared feature.

options.A: Incorrect. Bond angles of about $109^\circ$ are tetrahedral and found in poly(ethene) where carbons are $sp^3$. Ethene is trigonal planar with angles of about $120^\circ$.
options.B: Incorrect. Ethene has one $\pi$ bond in its $C=C$ double bond. This $\pi$ bond breaks during polymerisation, so poly(ethene) contains only $\sigma$ bonds and no $\pi$ bonds.
options.C: Correct. Both contain $\sigma$ covalent bonds. Ethene has $\sigma$ bonds in $C-H$ and in the $C-C$ framework plus a $\pi$ bond, while poly(ethene) has only $\sigma$ bonds in all its $C-H$ and $C-C$ single bonds.
options.D: Incorrect. $sp^3$ orbitals are found in poly(ethene) with its four $\sigma$ bonds per carbon. Ethene uses $sp^2$ orbitals with one unhybridised p orbital left for the $\pi$ bond.
